title: Holi: the Lord in the pillar
hook: Prahlad says the Lord is even in a stone pillar; his father strikes it, and Narasimha bursts out
carry: the lord is in the pillar, and in everyone
tomorrow: Maha Shivaratri: the great night of Shiva

segments.voice: Yesterday: Diwali and King Bali, a demon king honored for keeping his word, who comes home once a year.

At the Holi bonfire, Prahlad walks out of the fire. But the story doesn't stop there, and the Bhagavata Purana carries it further. His father, the king Hiranyakashipu, has tried everything to kill him, and nothing works. Finally, in a rage, he stands before his son in the great hall and asks: this Vishnu of yours, who you say is everywhere. Is he in this pillar? The boy says yes. And the king strikes the pillar.
screen: `THE FIRE WAS NOT THE END.` → `IS HE IN THIS PILLAR?` → `THE KING STRIKES IT.`

segments.voice: To understand what happens next, you need the king's boon. Long before, after fierce austerities, Hiranyakashipu had been granted protection, as the Bhagavata tells it, with a long list of conditions. No man or animal could kill him. Not by day or by night. Not inside or outside. Not on the earth or in the sky. Not with any weapon. He thought he'd closed every door. When he strikes the pillar, it splits open, and out comes Narasimha: Vishnu as half man, half lion. Neither man nor animal. He seizes the king at twilight, neither day nor night; on the threshold of the hall, neither inside nor outside; across his lap, neither earth nor sky; and ends him with his claws, which are not a weapon. Narasimha's fury is so terrible that even the gods are afraid to come near. They send the boy. Prahlad bows, and Narasimha calms and puts his hand on his head. Offered any blessing, Prahlad asks that his father, who tried to kill him again and again, be purified and freed, and the Bhagavata says it is granted. Under the whole story sits one of Hinduism's biggest teachings: the Lord isn't only in the temple or in heaven. He is in everything, so fully that he can step out of a stone column. Many teachers read Prahlad's wish the same way: if the Lord is in everyone, he is in the father who hurt him too. That's why Holi's fire is for Prahlad, and its morning is for visiting, making up, and putting color on old rivals as well as friends.
screen: `NOT MAN OR BEAST, NOT DAY OR NIGHT.` · `NARASIMHA BURSTS FROM THE PILLAR.` · `ONLY THE BOY CAN CALM HIM.` · `THE LORD IS IN EVERYTHING.` · then, large: `EVEN IN THE PILLAR. EVEN IN HIM.`

segments.voice: Bring back the small grudge from the fire a couple of weeks ago, or a new one. Try Prahlad's way, just a little: picture the Lord, or simply the good, present in that person too, the way he was present in the pillar. Then, for one breath, wish them free of whatever made them act that way. If you pray, say it to Narasimha. Let it go with the out-breath.
Holi. The fire for Prahlad, Narasimha from the pillar, and a boy who saw the Lord even in the father who hurt him.
Your line: the Lord is in the pillar, and in everyone. Tomorrow, a column of fire with no end. Rest well.

howItsDone: At Holika Dahan, some communities roast ears of new wheat or barley in the bonfire and share them; the next morning, Holi is often a day for visiting, reconciling and starting fresh with neighbors and relatives.
